correctness.rationale: For every integer p>=3, explicit Fourier orthogonality gives p exact 2x2 blocks with a necessary swap at the cyclic boundary. Gaussian polar coordinates reduce the log determinant to twice a sum of iid log Gamma(shape 2) radii and a cyclic sum of uniform-angle logs. Conditional Haar invariance gives vanishing cross-covariances. Gamma digamma/trigamma identities yield exact finite p mean p(1-2 gamma-log4) and variance p(2 pi^2/3-3). Removing one boundary term leaves a one-dependent stationary sequence with finite moments and positive long-run variance, proving the stated CLT; Chebyshev gives the geometric-volume limit. The original full matrix and derived product were compared in the saved checker (254 recorded checks).

value.rationale: The determinant of a square Gabor synthesis matrix is a natural geometric measure of global analysis-map volume. For a minimal two-translation and half-modulation critical design, the proof identifies an exact finite-size mean, an exact variance affected by reuse of random coordinates, and a growing-dimensional normal fluctuation law. These give a quantitative typical-case invariant not supplied by the structural block theorem or generic frame-bound estimates; no unmotivated parameter slice or condition-number consequence is claimed.
